title: Malachi questions God’s love — Malachi 1
paragraphs: Malachi questions God’s love — Malachi 1

He didn’t deny God.
He doubted His love.
That’s heavier.
In Book of Malachi 1, the people look at God and ask, “How have You loved us?”

Not atheism.
Not rebellion.
Just a tired, wounded question.
“Show me.”

Because life didn’t look like love.
Crops failing.
Worship dry.
Promises delayed.
And silence can feel like absence.
But God answers—not with emotion, but with history.

“I have loved you,” says the Lord.
Then He points to Jacob and Esau.

Not feelings.
Covenant.

Not a moment.
A story.
But here’s what we miss…

They were measuring God’s love by their current comfort.
God was revealing His love through His eternal choice.

They wanted proof now.
God gave them proof before they were even born.
And we do the same.

We say, “God, if You love me, fix this.”
He says, “I already proved it at the cross.”
Because the loudest answer to Malachi 1 isn’t in Malachi.
It’s in Jesus.

On that hill, outside Jerusalem—
where the Son was not spared—
where grace bled for the guilty—
That’s where the question dies.
“How have You loved us?”

Sin deserved distance.
Christ brought us near.

Doubt whispered, “You’re forgotten.”
The cross thundered, “You are chosen.”
So if your heart is asking that same question tonight…

Don’t just look at your situation.
Look at your Savior.

Because love isn’t always loud in the moment—
but it is undeniable in redemption.
From question to cross—because Jesus already answered it.
